- Builds maintainer ruling A (6915086281) on #33724: the Turso REMOTE face answers `relax_not_null: 'applied'` and relaxes the column in place with libSQL `ALTER TABLE … ALTER COLUMN … TO …`, in one write batch with a check that `sqlite_master.sql` equals the planned SQL (mismatch rolls back), applied only on a nullable read-back with the same type, DEFAULT and pk. No rebuild fall-back. Dev reports 6917853648 and 6919701288 on #33724.
- Declaration: `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. +830/-72; tests outside driver-turso by claim amendment 6917885070.
- Check-runs on this head: 38 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure (all Test Core shards green).
- ⚠ The PR stays draft and will not land until ruling parameter 4's first step is measured: the real-sqld pin (`turso-remote-relax-not-null-sqld.test.ts`, gated on `OS_TEST_SQLD_BIN`) could not run in the seat container, and the route is with the maintainer. If sqld refuses the statement, the card goes back to him and this head may change; I will send a delta then. Reviewing now saves the queue time.
- Points to read: the comma refusal (libSQL's splice ends the old definition at the first comma, so such a column is refused whole and left byte-identical); the in-batch check plus rollback on a face with no transactions (ADR-0119 D1); the advisory `object-column-changes-not-applied` still covered by a refused relax.
